name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
grip: Overhand pronated grip with palms facing down and thumbs wrapped around the barbell, hands shoulder-width apart.
description: Extend the wrists upward against a barbell while forearms rest flat along a bench or thighs, isolating the forearm extensor muscles on the top of the forearm.
setup: Sit on the side of a flat bench or kneel beside it with a lightweight barbell.
Rest your forearms flat across the bench pad (or your thighs) with wrists hanging just over the edge.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand pronated grip (palms facing downward), hands shoulder-width apart.
instructions: Lower the barbell by flexing your wrists downward until you feel a comfortable stretch in the forearm extensors.
Raise the barbell by extending your wrists upward as high as possible, contracting the extensor muscles on the top of your forearms.
Keep your forearms firmly glued to the bench pad throughout the entire motion (do not lift elbows).
Pause briefly at peak extension, then slowly lower the bar back to the starting stretch.
cues: Keep forearms glued to the bench.
Extend knuckles upward toward the ceiling.
commonMistakes: Lifting the elbows or forearms off the bench to assist the lift.
Using excessive weight that restricts wrist range of motion.
Bouncing or rolling the bar across the fingers.

logging.example: Light barbell loaded to 15 kg: record 15 kg total barbell mass.
logging.note: Wrist extensors are small muscle groups requiring modest loads; record total loaded barbell mass.

variantNote: Pronated forearm-supported wrist extension targeting the extensor carpi group. Direct counterpart to the supinated barbell wrist curl.
